chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Al-Walid ibn Uqba was witnessed with the drinking of wine, Uthman said to Ali (peace be upon him),
Judge between him and those who alleged that he drank wine.
So Ali (peace be upon him) ordered, and he was whipped with a whip that had two strands, forty lashes.
ai.seo_question: What was the specific penalty and method of execution for drinking wine as narrated in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the judicial practice of Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) in adjudicating the case of Al-Walid ibn Uqba, a prominent Umayyad governor known for his public consumption of wine. The ruling specifies forty lashes administered with a two-stranded whip, reflecting the classical Shia interpretation of the *hadd* penalty for *shurb al-khamr* (drinking wine) as distinct from other forms of corporal punishment. This narration underscores the authority of the Imams in implementing Islamic law and provides a concrete example of how *hadd* penalties were executed in early Islamic society.
